At WK Kellogg Co, we exist to create joy and connection to inspire Gr-r-reat days. We believe that doing good is always good for business and we have stood for this since Kellogg Company was founded more than 120 years ago. We are passionate about doing our part to make nutritious foods, create social connectivity and respect natural resources. Together, these actions create positive progress for people and the planet – today and for years to come. We have big plans for how we are going to accomplish this, and we would love for you to join us in this effort.
  
  
**The most compelling leadership opportunities aren’t always about stepping into something already built. Sometimes they’re about helping shape what comes next.**
The
**Senior Manager, Plant Operations**
leads the strategic and operational direction of multiple business units within a high-performing, large-scale, 24/7 manufacturing operation, and line-centric manufacturing platform.
  
  
This role drives excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people development by empowering Operations Managers, Supervisors, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.
  
  
**You won’t simply inherit an operation. You’ll have the opportunity to help build what comes next.**
**Working Relationships Include**

* Reports to: Plant Director
* Supervises: Operations Managers and Supervisors
* Peer Relationships: KSUM, Quality Manager, Sr. RM Manager, HR Manager, EHS Manager, E& F Manager, KIWS Coach
* Key Contacts: Internal – Plant Leadership Team, Corporate Operations, Engineering, KIWS, HR; External – Vendors, Contractors, and Corporate Support Functions

**Here’s What You Will Be Doing**

* Strategic Leadership: Set direction and priorities for assigned business units, ensuring alignment with plant goals and corporate strategy.
* Team Development: Lead, coach, and develop Operations Managers and Supervisor to build high-performing teams and future leaders.
* Operational Oversight: Ensure consistent execution of production plans and consistently deliver strong results across key plant KPIs, including safety, quality, food safety, cost, and service.
* Innovation & Project Execution: Lead the excellent execution of innovation and projects entering the plant, ensuring effective planning, cross-functional alignment, and successful implementation.
* Budgeting & Planning: Own the business planning and budgeting process for assigned units, including cost containment and resource allocation.
* Lean & CI Deployment: Champion and sustain lean manufacturing principles and WK Kellogg Integrated Work Systems (KIWS) across all units.
* Culture & Engagement: Drive a culture of safety, accountability, and engagement, promoting continuous learning and recognition.
* Compliance & Standards: Ensure compliance with all regulatory and internal standards related to safety, food safety, sanitation, and labor relations.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with support functions and external stakeholders to optimize performance and resolve complex challenges.

**Work Environment**

* This role is based within a 24/7 union manufacturing facility.
* Must be flexible to work any shift and travel up to 25%
* Regular presence on the production floor required
* Frequent interaction with internal teams and external partners

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required
* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing
* Proven success in leading large teams and managing multiple production lines
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement systems
* Demonstrated ability to lead through others and build effective teams
* Excellent strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
* Experience in union environments preferred
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and SAP
* Experience with budget creation and performance management
* Experience working within a 24/7 manufacturing environment is preferred

*$164,160 - $205,200*

**Job Description**
As an S&C Electric team member, you’ll work on projects that have real-world impact. You’ll help transform the grid for resilient and reliable power worldwide. S&C has more than a 100-year history of innovation and has been 100% employee-owned since 2012. We continue this legacy as a trusted, forward-thinking leader in the electrical industry. You will advance a safer, more reliable, and more resilient electrical grid. Our products help the grid adapt to severe weather and transition to clean energy. We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively. Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner.
  
  
**Hours**

* 8:00 am – 5:00 pm (Mon-Fri) On Site Palatine, IL

**Compensation**
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices.
**The estimated annual base salary range for this position is $154,968- $205,332.60.**
Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
  
  
**Join Our Team as a Senior Manager – Productions Operations!**
The Senior Manager – Production Operations is responsible for planning, overseeing, and managing the operations and production processes for the department, leading a team of Managers, Assistant Managers, and Supervisors to achieve strategic Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC). The Senior Manager – Production Operations focuses on strategic and tactical operations planning with a mid-term focus, contributing towards greater functional strategies, directing the smooth operations of multiple departments, driving strategic problem-solving and continuous improvement initiatives, reporting out to executive leadership on results, and making strategic adjustments and countermeasures when targets are missed.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Health & Safety Compliance: Drive a safety-first culture, ensuring leaders understand and enforce safety rules. Ensure that health & safety is considered in all departmental plans in order to maintain and promote a safety-conscious manufacturing environment and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards related to production operations.
* Leadership & People Management: Lead, inspire, and develop a high-performing team. Role model appropriate and professional workplace behaviors, address/mediate conflicts to restore harmony, and support a positive, healthy, and inclusive workplace culture in accordance with S&C's mission, vision, values, and guiding principles. Manage departmental administrative team member processes, including but not limited to recruitment, induction, vacation management, performance reviews, performance improvement plans, and workforce/succession planning. Proactively establish, monitor, and hold team members accountable to clear responsibilities and accountabilities; provide ongoing performance feedback, both positive and developmental; address performance gaps in a timely manner; recognize and reward achievements and initiate decisions for corrective actions and terminations where required. Foster a culture that supports the growth and development of team members and proactively train, mentor, and coach team members.
* Strategy Implementation: Cascade strategies to develop mid-term tactical and operational plans for the function, in line with the company’s overall business objectives, including automation, insourcing, and unattended machining. Oversee a leadership team that directs the day-to-day operations of activities within the department and span of control, ensuring the timely and cost-effective delivery of outputs to KPIs. Work with senior leaders to recommend and implement strategic adjustments to operational plans in order to meet OKRs and KPIs.
* Production Planning & Operations: Lead strategic production planning initiatives, collaborating with cross-functional teams to develop a mid-term plan for the department and initiate strategies that contribute to long-term production planning. Work with leaders to optimize production schedules, identify bottlenecks, and determine capacity plans and processing methods. Evaluate machine resources to ensure continued production and minimal downtime. Establish a balance between increased productivity and reduced costs of manufacturing operations. Set mid-term productivity goals and analyze report-outs from Managers.
* Lean Performance Systems: Recommend and implement goals for departmental performance improvement, supporting leaders as they identify and implement process improvements to enhance production efficiency, reduce costs, and increase overall operational effectiveness. Collaborate with other leaders to formulate high-level solutions and develop plans for how to implement improvements throughout multi-faceted functions. Serve as a change agent by influencing, communicating, and institutionalizing a culture of continuous improvement, simplification, standard work, process improvement, and lean principles.
* Quality Management: Oversee the implementation of broad quality control programs, ensuring leaders fully understand quality issues and their corresponding solutions.Discuss and understand high-level, multi-faceted quality issues and help leaders formulate resolutions. Monitor and guide leaders responsible for the department’s communication of corrective action plans, resolutions, and quality results.
* Reporting: Analyzes reports and reviews provided by first-line supervisors. Communicates regularly with upper management regarding problems impacting production. Reports issues regarding production, quality, maintenance, or personnel to senior and executive leadership.
* Budget Management: Develop and manage the function’s budget, ensuring accuracy and appropriate allocation of resources to maximize ROI and the achievement of larger functional strategies and objectives. Approve expenditures for the achievement of operational goals and work with senior leaders to identify investment opportunities for gains towards mid-term goals.
* Compliance: Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
* Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
* Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
* Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
* Drive a car or other vehicle.
* Other responsibilities as assigned.

**Required**
**What you’ll need to succeed:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline such as Engineering, or a related field.
* Beliefs in, and alignment with, S&C Guiding Principles and Core Values
* 10+ years of manufacturing experience in an industrial metals fabrication environment, including advanced CNC machining, welding, laser cutting, forming, punching, stamping and related finishing operations.
* 5+ years of supervisory or management experience in a fabrication environment leading hourly and salaried employees.
* Leadership experience in workforce planning, scheduling, and staffing, employee development, coaching, and performance management.Experience managing multiple shifts is preferred.
* Knowledge of precision machining processes and practices within a high mix, low-to-medium volume environment.
* Demonstrated track record of lean manufacturing leadership, sustained improvements, and KPI attainment.
* Great leadership skills within a multi-level manufacturing environment, with an ability to lead, guide, motivate, and delegate to deliver results.
* Sound critical thinking, organizational, planning, and project management skills, and creative problem-solving when obstacles arise.
* Great interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect, navigate and resolve conflict, moderate behaviors, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.
* Excellent communication skills, (written, verbal, listening, and presentation) ability to liaise with internal and external stakeholders at all levels, from leadership to support staff, and present influentially to achieve buy-in from executives, managers, and team members.
* Sound analytical skills with the ability to use and analyze data to drive informed decisions, problem-solve difficult issues, and leverage data and learnings to drive continuous improvement.
* Proven success partnering across teams, creating effective partnerships at all levels, and collaborating at an operational level.
* Adapts to change and different ways of doing things quickly and positively and finds ways to get things accomplished, even when faced with challenges.
* Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook) and preferably, Oracle.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Six Sigma Certification(s).
* Certified Lean Six Sigma (CLSS).
* Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).

S&C Electric is committed to equal-opportunity employment. All employees and applicants will be considered without regard to age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law. If you are an individual with a disability and need an accommodation to complete the application, please email us at TAsupport@sandc.com.
  
  
No fixed deadline
  
  
**About Us**
In 1909, S&C Electric Company transformed the delivery of safe, reliable electricity with the invention of the Liquid Power Fuse. Today, as the world faces extreme weather events and the demand for electricity grows, S&C continues to innovate and advance the electrical grid, ensuring reliable and resilient power for homes, communities, and critical infrastructure around the world.
  
  
With a diverse, global workforce and core values around integrity, safety, and quality, S&C is a trusted industry leader and top workplace that offers meaningful careers to more than 3,500 team members. As a people-first organization, S&C is committed to fostering an inclusive and collaborative workplace where team members advance their careers through robust talent-development programs and involved leadership.
  
  
S&C’s deeply rooted belief diversity fosters greater creativity, innovation, and success guides the company to advance and sustain a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace culture.
  
  
**S&C provides a comprehensive and competitive benefit package that includes the following (eligibility requirements apply):**

* Health and Welfare Benefits: Medical & Prescription, Dental, Vision, Health Care and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, , Health Savings Account (HSA), Group Life Insurance, optional Supplemental Life and AD&D Insurance, Wellbeing Resources including Employee Assistance Program and Family Forming Benefits (i.e., Adoption and Fertility support)
* Leave Benefits: Vacation Time, Sick Time, Paid Holidays and Company Shutdown days, Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability, Other Leaves, Paid Parental Time and Military Leave

Retirement Benefits: 401(k) Retirement Savings and Employee Stock Ownership Plan (KSOP) offering traditional and Roth 401(k) options and an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) component; KSOP participants can receive annual ESOP company contributions of over 11% of eligible earnings (3% Core, up to 3.5% Match, Variable Periodic).

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, LEU+ Manufacturing Process Engineering
existing_roles.description:
Are you interested in being part of an innovative team that supports Westinghouse's mission to provide clean energy solutions? At Westinghouse, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset and we seek to identify, attract and recruit the most qualified talent while recognizing and encouraging the value of diversity in the global workplace.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Senior Manager, LEU+ Manufacturing Process Engineering, you will lead process engineering. This role is part of the LEU+ Manufacturing Program, a capital expansion of Westinghouse's Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility. The program aims to manufacture LEU+ (higher-enrichment low-enriched uranium) nuclear fuel. Accountable for the design, qualification and startup of the new manufacturing processes, including uranium conversion, pellet production, fuel rod and assembly manufacturing, uranium recovery and recycling, and the laboratory and maintenance areas. Plan and direct the methods, equipment and processes needed to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective fuel, and develops the engineers who deliver them.
  
  
You will report to the Project Director, LEU+ Manufacturing Program and be located at Columbia, SC. You will support this role 100% onsite.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the LEU+ Process Engineering organization with responsibility for safety, regulatory compliance, product quality, technical execution, cost, schedule, and operational readiness.
* Lead process engineering activities supporting nuclear safety, including Integrated Safety Analysis, hazard analysis, IROFS, criticality safety, NRC licensing activities, and regulatory change control.
* Oversee process engineering deliverables from initial design through equipment procurement, installation, commissioning, qualification, startup, and turnover to Operations.
* Ensure manufacturing equipment and processes meet product quality, nuclear safety, performance, and qualification requirements.
* Lead mechanical, chemical, and process engineering resources while forecasting staffing needs and assigning technical ownership.
* Coordinate technical interfaces across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Procurement, Construction, Commissioning, Automation/IT, and suppliers.
* Manage process engineering scope, budget, schedule, risks, and change control while providing clear status reporting to program leadership.
* Guide manufacturing optimization using Lean/Six Sigma, OEE, capacity analysis, bottleneck reduction, and continuous improvement.
* Support operational readiness through procedures, training, spare-parts planning, startup support, and turnover of qualified manufacturing processes.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical, Mechanical, Nuclear Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in process engineering, manufacturing, plant operations, capital projects, or related technical leadership.
* 5+ years of people-management experience leading engineers and managing technical resources and budgets.
* Demonstrated leadership of complex, diverse engineering or manufacturing programs with accountability for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and technical performance.
* Knowledge of process engineering, process safety, hazard analysis, manufacturing systems, and equipment/process qualification.
* Experience managing complex capital projects from design through commissioning, qualification, and operational readiness.
* Experience in nuclear fuel, nuclear materials, chemical processing, or a similarly regulated manufacturing environment.
* Knowledge of 10 CFR Part 70, Integrated Safety Analysis, nuclear safety controls, and regulatory change control.
* Knowledge of nuclear fuel manufacturing processes, including conversion, pelleting, rod/assembly manufacturing, or uranium recovery, preferred.
* Demonstrated experience with project controls, resource planning, budgeting, risk management, and change control.
* Experience developing leaders, building technical teams, and influencing across functional and organizational boundaries.
* Experience delivering continuous improvement and financial results without compromising safety, quality, or regulatory compliance.
* Lean Six Sigma experience required

We are committed to transparency and equity in all of our people practices. The base salary range for this position, which is dependent upon experience, qualifications and skills, is estimated to be $144,000 to $180,000 per year.
  
  
**Why Westinghouse?**
**Benefits**
**Our benefits package is tailored to meet the diverse needs of our employees, while also promoting wellness and career growth. The following are representative of what we offer:**

* Comprehensive Medical benefits which could include medical, dental, vision, prescription coverage and Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contributions options
* Wellness Programs designed to support employees in maintaining their health and well-being including Employee Assistance Program providing support for our employees and their household members
* 401(k) with Company Match Contributions to support employees' retirement
* Paid Vacations and Company Holidays
* Opportunities for Flexible Work Arrangements to promote work-life balance
* Educational Reimbursement and Comprehensive Career Programs to help employees grow in their careers

existing_roles.description:
Crusoe is on a mission
*to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence*
. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.
  
  
We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.
  
  
We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.
  
  
If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.
  
  
**About This Role:**
The
**Senior Manager, Quality Management Systems (QMS)**
will lead the development, implementation, governance, and continuous improvement of Crusoe's enterprise Quality Management System across multiple manufacturing facilities, supplier operations, subcontractors, and field deployment activities.
  
  
This individual will be responsible for establishing a scalable, standardized, risk-based QMS that enables consistent product quality, manufacturing process control, regulatory and customer compliance, and operational excellence across the organization.
  
  
The role will provide strategic and operational leadership for QMS governance, internal and external audits, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), document and records management, quality processes, compliance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  
  
The Senior Manager will lead and develop a team of QMS professionals, auditors, and documentation specialists while partnering closely with Product Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Supplier Quality, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Field Quality leadership.
  
  
The ideal candidate brings 10+ years of progressive Quality Management System experience, including substantial people-management experience in complex manufacturing environments. This individual must be capable of translating quality standards and business requirements into practical operating processes that improve manufacturing effectiveness, prevent defects, reduce operational risks, and support organizational growth.
  
  
**The ultimate objective is to establish a proactive, business-enabling QMS that drives consistency, accountability, compliance, and continuous improvement across Crusoe's growing AI Data Center infrastructure manufacturing and deployment ecosystem.**
**What You'll Be Working On:**

* Enterprise QMS Strategy, Governance & Leadership

+ Own and lead the enterprise Quality Management System strategy, architecture, implementation, and continuous improvement.
+ Establish and maintain a scalable QMS aligned with ISO 9001:2015 and applicable customer, regulatory, contractual, and industry requirements.
+ Develop standardized Quality policies, procedures, processes, work instructions, forms, and records applicable across all manufacturing facilities and operational functions.
+ Establish QMS governance, process ownership, accountability matrices, escalation mechanisms, and management review processes.
+ Ensure consistent implementation of Quality Management System requirements across Brighton, Tulsa-1, Tulsa-2, Arvada, Ponchatoula, and other future manufacturing and operational locations.
+ Establish a process-based, risk-oriented approach to quality management rather than a documentation-driven compliance culture.
+ Partner with Quality leadership to establish annual QMS objectives, strategic initiatives, resource plans, and performance targets.
+ Lead QMS maturity assessments and develop roadmaps to strengthen process effectiveness and organizational readiness.
+ Ensure QMS requirements are appropriately integrated into product development, manufacturing, supplier management, and field operations.

* ISO Compliance & Audit Management

+ Own the enterprise internal and external audit program, including audit planning, scheduling, execution, reporting, and follow-up.
+ Maintain organizational readiness for ISO 9001 certification, surveillance audits, recertification audits, and customer or third-party audits.
+ Lead and oversee internal audits across manufacturing, engineering, procurement, supplier quality, production, inspection, testing, and field operations.
+ Ensure audit programs evaluate actual process implementation and effectiveness rather than merely verifying documentation.
+ Manage relationships with external certification bodies, registrars, customer auditors, and regulatory or industry assessment organizations.
+ Establish risk-based audit schedules considering process criticality, historical performance, operational changes, and previous audit findings.
+ Ensure audit findings are appropriately classified, assigned, investigated, corrected, and closed within established timelines.
+ Verify corrective action effectiveness and prevent recurrence of systemic audit findings.
+ Develop and maintain qualified internal auditor resources across multiple facilities and functions.

* CAPA, Nonconformance & Continuous Improvement

+ Establish and govern enterprise-wide CAPA, nonconformance, deviation, and quality escalation processes.
+ Ensure effective root cause analysis using structured methodologies such as 5 Why, Fishbone, 8D, fault tree analysis, and other appropriate problem-solving techniques.
+ Drive accountability for corrective and preventive actions across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Supplier Quality, and Operations.
+ Monitor CAPA aging, overdue actions, recurrence rates, effectiveness verification, and systemic trends.
+ Identify recurring process failures, systemic weaknesses, and opportunities for organizational improvement.
+ Establish standardized requirements for nonconformance documentation, containment, disposition, investigation, and closure.
+ Lead cross-functional improvement initiatives that reduce process variation, eliminate waste, improve first-pass yield, and strengthen manufacturing process effectiveness.
+ Ensure lessons learned from internal defects, supplier issues, customer complaints, and field failures are incorporated into the QMS.

* QMS Documentation & Records Management

+ Own enterprise document and records management governance.
+ Establish standardized requirements for document creation, review, approval, release, revision control, distribution, retention, and obsolescence.
+ Ensure controlled management of Quality Manuals, policies, procedures, SOPs, work instructions, inspection plans, test procedures, forms, and quality records.
+ Implement effective document control processes across multiple facilities and functional organizations.
+ Ensure personnel have access to current and approved documentation at the point of use.
+ Establish document ownership and periodic review requirements.
+ Eliminate uncontrolled documentation, obsolete work instructions, inconsistent forms, and duplicate processes.
+ Drive adoption and effective utilization of electronic QMS platforms and digital document management solutions.
+ Ensure objective evidence and records are maintained to demonstrate process conformity and effectiveness.

* Risk Management & Operational Quality Governance

+ Establish enterprise-level Quality risk management processes.
+ Ensure risk-based thinking is incorporated into business processes, product realization, supplier management, manufacturing operations, and field activities.
+ Oversee QMS-related risk assessments and coordinate with functional leaders on DFMEA, PFMEA, process risk assessments, and operational controls.
+ Establish escalation mechanisms for significant Quality risks, process deviations, regulatory concerns, and potential customer impacts.
+ Ensure changes to products, processes, suppliers, equipment, and organizational structures are appropriately evaluated for QMS impact.
+ Drive management review processes that evaluate QMS performance, organizational risks, customer satisfaction, audit results, CAPA effectiveness, and improvement opportunities.

* Multi-Site Standardization & Deployment

+ Establish a consistent enterprise QMS framework while allowing controlled, documented site-specific requirements where necessary.
+ Lead QMS deployment, implementation, and maturity improvement across existing and new manufacturing facilities.
+ Partner with site Quality leaders to ensure standardized processes are effectively implemented and sustained.
+ Conduct periodic site assessments to evaluate QMS effectiveness, process adherence, and compliance maturity.
+ Establish cross-site benchmarking and sharing of best practices.
+ Ensure new manufacturing facilities and acquired or outsourced operations are incorporated into the enterprise QMS framework.
+ Develop standardized QMS deployment and operational readiness plans for new facilities.

* Customer, Supplier & Regulatory Quality Support

+ Partner with Supplier Quality leadership to ensure QMS requirements are incorporated into supplier qualification, supplier audits, corrective actions, and supplier performance management.
+ Ensure subcontractors and outsourced manufacturing partners operate under appropriate Quality requirements and controls.
+ Support customer audits, quality assessments, and contractual compliance requirements.
+ Ensure effective management of customer complaints, quality escapes, and external nonconformances through the enterprise CAPA framework.
+ Partner with Product and Manufacturing Quality to ensure appropriate quality planning and process controls are established.
+ Maintain awareness of applicable industry standards, regulatory requirements, and customer-specific Quality requirements relevant to electrical and mechanical infrastructure manufacturing.

* People Leadership & Organizational Development

+ Build, lead, and develop a high-performing QMS organization.
+ Directly manage QMS personnel, including QMS Leads, Quality Auditors, QMS Documentation Specialists, and other assigned Quality professionals.
+ Establish clear roles, responsibilities, performance expectations, and individual development plans.
+ Conduct regular one-on-ones, performance reviews, talent assessments, and succession planning.
+ Develop technical and leadership competencies within the QMS organization.
+ Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement.
+ Establish effective working relationships with site Quality leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.
+ Identify resource requirements and develop headcount and organizational plans to support current and future business growth.
+ Mentor and develop future Quality leaders and technical subject matter experts.

* Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Establishing, monitoring, and improving measurable QMS performance indicators, including:

+ QMS Compliance
+ Audit Management
+ CAPA Effectiveness
+ Document Control
+ Multi-Site Standardization
+ Process Effectiveness
+ Organizational Development
+ Customer Quality
+ Continuous Improvement

**What You'll Bring to the Team:**

* Educational Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Industrial Technology, or a related technical discipline.
* Professional Experience:

+ 7+ Years of Dedicated Experience in QMS, plus additional experience in Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Quality, or Quality Assurance.
+ 5+ Years of People Leadership Experience: Including managing and developing Quality professionals and technical teams (these years may overlap with the 10+ above).

* QMS Expertise: Demonstrated experience owning, implementing, and improving enterprise or multi-site Quality Management Systems.
* ISO 9001 Expertise: Strong working knowledge of ISO 9001:2015 requirements and certification processes.
* Core Quality Methodologies: Demonstrated expertise in CAPA, root cause analysis, nonconformance management, and continuous improvement.
* Quality Documentation & Document Control: Experience developing and implementing Quality policies, procedures, SOPs, work instructions, and document control systems.
* Cross-Functional Leadership: Experience managing cross-functional Quality initiatives across Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, and Supply Chain.
* Risk & Process Management: Strong understanding of risk-based thinking, process management, and operational excellence.
* eQMS Implementation: Experience implementing or administering electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS).
* Influence & Accountability: Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and drive organizational accountability without relying solely on hierarchical authority.
* Communication & Analytical Skills: Excellent written, verbal, analytical, organizational, and presentation skills.
* Travel: Willingness to travel 25–40% of the time, based on business needs.
* Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility; drug and alcohol program participation is required. Must be able to pass a background check.

**Bonus Points:**

* Advanced Education: Master's degree in Engineering, Quality, Operations Management, or Business Administration.
* Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Manager (CMQ/OE), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or equivalent professional credentials.
* Lead Auditor Certification: ISO 9001 Lead Auditor certification.
* Industry Experience: Experience in electrical equipment, switchgear, switchboards, power distribution, mechanical assemblies, data center infrastructure, aerospace, automotive, energy, or other complex manufacturing industries.
* Industry Standards: Familiarity with UL 891, UL 508, applicable IEC, IEEE, NEMA, NFPA, and other relevant industry standards.
* Multi-Site QMS Deployment: Experience managing QMS deployment across multiple manufacturing facilities and outsourced manufacturing operations.
* Digital Quality Systems: Experience with digital QMS platforms, ERP integration, document management, and quality analytics.
* Lean & Six Sigma: Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and operational excellence methodologies.
* NPI & Scale-Up: Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI), manufacturing scale-up, and new facility launches.

**Benefits:**

* Competitive compensation and equity packages
* Restricted Stock Units
* Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs
* Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance
* Employer contributions to HSA account
* Paid parental leave
* Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability
* Professional development & tuition reimbursement
* Mental health & wellness support
* Commuter benefits (parking & transit)
* Cell phone stipend
* 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary
* Volunteer time off
* Global travel insurance & emergency assistance
* Daily meals allowance
* Additional perks & programs specific to location

**Compensation:**
Compensation will be paid in the range of $190,000 - $215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

This role builds and leads the plant-level QA/QC team, who will report directly to it. It holds quality stop-work authority and provides independent verification across facilities. The Senior Manager partners with the Harris corporate QA/QC program, applying and extending it to manufacturing, and works with Manufacturing Operations, Engineering and VDC, Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, and Safety. The role standardizes quality practices and supports certification of new facilities as the network scales.
  
  
**Core Responsibilities**
**Quality Management System & Certifications**

* Own the manufacturing certification programs, including ISO 9001 and ASME, with documentation, internal audits, and management review.
* Lead certification and recertification for new and existing facilities, including customer and third-party audits.
* Align manufacturing procedures with the Harris corporate QMS manual and manage manufacturing-specific procedures and records.
* Drive consistent quality system implementation across the network.
* Represent Harris in professional and industry organizations.

**Plant QA/QC Leadership & Inspection**

* Build, staff, and lead the plant-level QA/QC team, including roles, hiring, training, and standards.
* Establish and own inspection, verification, and hold/release processes, from receiving through final inspection.
* Define inspection plans and travelers by product and customer requirement.
* Ensure welding procedures and welder qualifications meet code, and manage calibration of inspection equipment.
* Manage third-party inspection firms and their scope, schedule, and results

**VDC Deliverable QA/QC Review**

* Spot-check VDC deliverables, including drawings, models, and BOMs, before they reach the shop, as an independent check on VDC's own QA/QC.
* Audit VDC's QA/QC process and record results, and raise gaps with VDC leadership.
* Track shop-found drawing, model, and BOM issues, and feed trends back to VDC and Engineering.
* Hold deliverables that fail verification until corrected.

**Nonconformance, Corrective Action & Quality Performance**

* Own the nonconformance (NCR) process, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive actions, including supplier issues.
* Track and report quality metrics, including rework, weld repair, NCR trends, and customer complaints.
* Work with Industrial Engineering and plant leadership to turn quality data into improvements.

**Quality Stop-Work Authority**

* Exercise stop-work authority when product, process, or documentation does not meet requirements, escalating to the SVP as needed.
* Define clear criteria for stop, hold, and release.

**Production Readiness & Supplier Quality**

* Set quality requirements, inspection and test plans, and documentation for new products and projects at the production readiness gate and manage 3rd party inspection companies.
* Partner with Supply Chain on supplier quality, receiving inspection, and material certifications.
* Support customer quality requirements and audits for external customers.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration**
**This Role Works Closely With**

* Harris corporate QA/QC program leadership
* Manufacturing Operations, Industrial Engineering, Safety
* Engineering, VDC, and Product Engineering
* Supply Chain, Purchasing, and Fulfillment & Logistics
* Manufacturing Business Development and Estimating
* Customers, auditors, and certification bodies

The Senior Manager owns the manufacturing quality system and independent verification. Plant leadership owns producing quality product in the shop.
  
  
**Required Qualifications**

* Experience building and leading quality assurance or quality control across multiple manufacturing, fabrication, or prefabrication facilities, including hiring and developing quality staff.
* Experience leading ISO 9001 and ASME or other code-based certification and recertification, including internal audits and corrective action.
* Experience with inspection, nonconformance management, and root cause analysis.
* Ability to read engineering drawings, specifications, and codes.
* Ability to hold plant leaders accountable while keeping production moving.
* Strong communication skills with customers, auditors, and cross-functional teams.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with nuclear quality assurance, ASME boiler and pressure vessel code, or other code-based quality programs.
* Professional Engineer (PE) license.
* Experience with welding, piping, structural, or modular MEP fabrication.
* Certifications such as CWI, ASQ CQE/CQA/CMQ, or Lead Auditor.
* Experience with quality and production tracking systems such as STRATUS.

**This Role Is**
**What This Role Is (and Is Not)**

* The enterprise owner of the manufacturing quality system and certifications.
* The builder and leader of plant-level QA/QC across facilities.
* The authority for inspection, hold/release, and quality stop-work.
* An independent check that protects customers and Harris' reputation as the network scales.

**This Role Is NOT**

* The owner of plant production or shop-floor output (Manufacturing Operations).
* The owner of the Harris corporate QA/QC program.
* The owner of VDC's internal QA/QC (VDC).
* Responsible for safety programs or safety stop-work (Safety).
* The owner of product design or productization (Product Engineering).

**Your life at Harris**
As one of the country's leading mechanical contractors, Harris offers you the best of both worlds: the stability, resources and opportunities of a national company, and the team culture, creative spirit and customer loyalty of a local business. If you thrive on variety and new challenges, we want to meet you!
  
  
From stadiums to manufacturing facilities, power plants to hospitals, concert halls to classrooms, we handle projects of all sizes and complexity from multiple regional locations across the country.
  
  
**Harris Benefits + Compensation**

* Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance
* 401K with company match
* Vacation time, sick time, and paid holidays
* Paid Parental leave
* Short-Term Incentive Plan

Visit our Careers Page for additional benefit details: https://www.harriscompany.com/careers/employee-benefits-at-a-glance

$111,060.64 - $166,590.97
  
  
The actual salary offer will vary by candidate based on a wide range of factors such as specific skills, qualifications, experience, and location.

**About Mach Industries**
Founded in 2023, Mach Industries is a rapidly growing defense technology company focused on developing next-generation autonomous defense platforms. At the core of our mission is the commitment to delivering scalable, decentralized defense systems that enhance the strategic capabilities of the United States and its allies. With a workforce of approximately 350 employees, we operate with startup agility and ambition.
  
  
Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.
  
  
**The Role**
Mach Industries is seeking a Principal Manufacturing Engineer, Energetics to lead the development and industrialization of manufacturing systems for solid rocket motors (SRMs), pyrotechnics, and energetic products.
  
  
This role will have end-to-end technical ownership of energetic manufacturing capability, from early manufacturing concepts and process architecture through facility buildout, equipment integration, commissioning, qualification, and production launch.
  
  
You will define how energetic products are manufactured at scale: translating product and process requirements into manufacturing cells, production lines, hazardous-process facilities, equipment specifications, controls architectures, material flows, and commissioning plans.
  
  
This is a highly cross-functional role requiring coordination across product engineering, manufacturing, automation, facilities, EHS, quality, operations, external A/E firms, equipment OEMs, and systems integrators.
  
  
The ideal candidate has personally taken complex manufacturing systems from concept through production and is comfortable operating as the technical DRI for large, multidisciplinary capital projects.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Manufacturing System & Line Design**

* Own the manufacturing architecture for solid rocket motor, pyrotechnic, and other energetic production lines from raw material receipt through finished-product acceptance.
* Translate product requirements and production targets into manufacturing processes, equipment requirements, cycle times, staffing models, material flows, and factory layouts.
* Develop process flows, equipment concepts, line balancing, capacity models, manufacturing requirements, and capital equipment roadmaps.
* Establish equipment boundaries, interfaces, utilities, controls requirements, inspection strategy, and material-handling concepts.
* Lead design reviews including process, equipment, layout, automation, operability, maintainability, and production-readiness reviews.
* Identify manufacturing bottlenecks and develop scalable production architectures capable of supporting significant rate increases.
* Drive Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) feedback into product development.

**Energetics Process Industrialization**

* Industrialize manufacturing processes associated with solid rocket motors and pyrotechnic products, including energetic material preparation, mixing, casting/dispensing, curing, machining, assembly, inspection, testing, and material handling.
* Translate development processes into robust, repeatable production processes with defined operating windows and acceptance criteria.
* Develop process specifications, manufacturing requirements, equipment URS documents, control plans, and qualification strategies.
* Partner with EHS and process safety teams to incorporate energetic-material hazards into equipment and process design.
* Drive reductions in operator exposure and manual handling through appropriate automation, remote operation, process isolation, and engineered controls.

**Facility & Infrastructure Buildout**

* Serve as the manufacturing technical owner for new energetic production facilities and major facility expansions.
* Translate manufacturing processes into facility requirements including equipment layouts, utilities, hazardous-area requirements, material flows, personnel flows, storage requirements, and operational constraints.
* Work directly with architects, A/E firms, general contractors, EHS, authorities having jurisdiction, and equipment integrators throughout facility design and construction.
* Participate in concept design, basis-of-design development, FEED, detailed design, construction, installation, and startup.
* Ensure facility design supports production throughput, equipment maintainability, future expansion, safe operations, and efficient material movement.
* Own manufacturing requirements and interfaces between the facility, process equipment, automation systems, utilities, and production operations.

**Capital Equipment & Integration**

* Develop technical specifications and requirements for custom and off-the-shelf manufacturing equipment.
* Lead equipment vendor and systems-integrator selection from technical evaluation through execution.
* Own technical execution of major manufacturing equipment programs including design reviews, fabrication, integration, installation, and acceptance.
* Work with automation engineers and integrators to define controls, robotics, machine vision, data acquisition, traceability, and manufacturing software requirements.
* Review and approve equipment designs for process capability, safety, serviceability, controls architecture, and production readiness.
* Manage technical interfaces across multiple equipment suppliers and integrators to ensure individual systems function as a complete manufacturing line.

**Commissioning & Production Launch**

* Own manufacturing equipment commissioning and line startup from installation through production release.
* Develop and execute equipment acceptance and commissioning strategies including FAT, SAT, commissioning, process qualification, and production-readiness activities.
* Lead equipment debugging, process characterization, capability studies, and production trials.
* Establish equipment and process acceptance criteria and drive closure of technical issues identified during commissioning.
* Partner with Quality to establish inspection strategies, process controls, traceability, and manufacturing acceptance criteria.
* Drive production ramp by identifying and eliminating constraints related to equipment reliability, cycle time, yield, scrap, ergonomics, and process capability.
* Transition manufacturing systems to site operations and maintenance teams with appropriate documentation, training, spare-parts strategies, and sustainment plans.

**Technical Leadership**

* Act as a senior technical authority for energetic manufacturing systems across Mach Industries.
* Lead multidisciplinary technical decisions spanning manufacturing, automation, facilities, process safety, quality, and operations.
* Develop manufacturing standards and reusable architectures for future energetic production facilities.
* Mentor manufacturing and automation engineers and raise the technical standard for capital equipment execution across the organization.
* Independently identify technical and program risks and drive them to resolution.
* Communicate manufacturing strategy, technical tradeoffs, capital requirements, schedule risks, and execution status to engineering and company leadership.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
* 10+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, process engineering, industrialization, factory engineering, or capital equipment development.
* Demonstrated ownership of complex manufacturing equipment or production lines from concept through installation, commissioning, and production.
* Experience developing manufacturing processes and translating them into equipment and facility requirements.
* Experience specifying, procuring, integrating, and commissioning capital equipment.
* Experience working with equipment OEMs, systems integrators, construction teams, and/or A/E firms.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing fundamentals including process capability, line balancing, equipment reliability, yield, throughput, and production ramp.
* Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical programs across multiple engineering disciplines with limited oversight.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Direct experience designing, building, commissioning, or operating solid rocket motor, propellant, pyrotechnic, ammunition, warhead, or other energetic-material manufacturing facilities.
* Experience with energetic processes such as material preparation, mixing, casting, dispensing, curing, machining, assembly, inspection, and testing.
* Experience taking an energetic manufacturing process from development or pilot scale into rate production.
* Experience with hazardous-process facility design and manufacturing equipment intended for explosive or energetic environments.
* Working knowledge of applicable explosives, fire protection, electrical, process safety, and DoD energetic-manufacturing requirements.
* Experience working with A/E and EPC organizations on greenfield or brownfield manufacturing facility projects.
* Experience developing equipment URS documents, RFQs/RFPs, statements of work, acceptance criteria, and capital project specifications.
* Experience executing FAT, SAT, commissioning, process qualification, and production acceptance.
* Experience with automated manufacturing equipment, PLC-controlled systems, robotics, machine vision, and manufacturing data systems.
* Experience building production systems within aerospace, defense, propulsion, munitions, automotive, semiconductor, chemical processing, or similarly demanding manufacturing environments.

**Additional Requirements**

* Available to work extended hours and weekends as needed

existing_roles.title: Chief Manufacturing Engineer-Remote
existing_roles.description:
**Fantastic challenges. Amazing opportunities.**
GKN Aerospace is reimagining air travel: going further, faster and greener! Fuelled by great people whose expertise and creativity sets the standards in our industry, we’re inspired by the opportunities to innovate and break boundaries. We’re proud to play a part in protecting the world’s democracies. And we’re committed to putting sustainability at the centre of everything we do, opening up and protecting our planet. With over 16,000 employees across 32 manufacturing sites in 12 countries we serve over 90% of the world’s aircraft and engine manufacturers and achieved sales of £3.6bn in 2025. There are no limits to where you can take your career.
  
  
Role Summary
  
  
As part of GKN Aerospace Airframes E&T, Chief Manufacturing Engineers (CME) lead the development, industrialisation and improvement of Manufacturing Systems whilst serving as the customer-facing representatives of the ME function.
  
  
Day-to-day, a CME is focused on delivery of non-recurring engineering projects including New Product Introductions (NPI), Transfers of Work (ToW), Major Modifications (Mods), Technology Insertions and resolving manufacturing process related quality and delivery challenges together with production engineering teams.
  
  
When necessary, a CME may lead deployed ME resources to deliver these projects, ensuring compliance with identified requirements (e.g. Produceability, Productivity, Cost, Schedule, Regulatory) and adherence to Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) standards.
  
  
**Remote Role**
Travel Requirements
  
  
This is a remote working position that requires frequent routine and occasional non-routine travel (up to 25-50%) to be on-site at GKN facilities and suppliers, including but not limited to; Phoenix (AZ), Wichita (KS), Sumner (WA), Chihuahua (Mexico), Tallassee (AL).
  
  
Candidates must live in a location with strong transport links. This could be 1-2 hours drive (approx.) from a major international hub airport (e.g. Dallas, Atlanta, Houston) or locally to a regional airport with multiple flights per day to major hub airports.
  
  
Role Accountabilities
  
  

* Bids– Accountable to validate and approve the proposed definition of the Manufacturing System and its associated performance targets which are submitted at LG3 (Programme Launch). Working closely with the Industrial Architect, the CME reviews output for technical risks and communicates these to the Programme. This may include process flow, bill of materials, proposed industrial setting, product cost estimates, requirements compliance or technology developments needed. The CME owns the Non-Recurring Engineering cost estimate for the ME technical content delivery.
* NPI– Accountable for delivering a Manufacturing System that fulfils all agreed stakeholder requirements (technical, quality, regulatory), business case metrics and system performance targets between LG3 (Programme Launch) and LG7 (Steady State Production) whilst ensuring that planning, development and commissioning is completed on-schedule and on-cost.
* Sustaining – Accountable for the governance and oversight of a portfolio of Manufacturing Systems, delivered through regular review of system KPIs and Industrial Review assessments. Takes corrective action to ensure Manufacturing Systems continue to perform in-line with the productivity & quality targets set.
* Leadership of Projects- Accountable for delivery of the non-recurring ME activities within a given programme or project. Responsible to provide technical leadership and direction using project management fundamentals: planning & estimating, resourcing & budgeting and reporting on project performance (earned value) to internal business standards.
* Leadership of Teams – Accountable to the Programme and Site for effective utilisation of deployed manufacturing engineering resource while delivering ME content of projects by providing day-to-day coordination, recognition and accountability and implementing ME best practice with the deployed team.
* Quality – Accountable for delivery of manufacturing systems that are Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) capable through a relentless focus on delivering APQP to the AS9145 standard during the NPI phase. Must exhibit and drive a product quality mind-set within ME and ensure compliance to agreed Customer, Regulatory, Business and functional standards.
* Relationships – Accountable to maintain positive and functional working relationships with internal and external customers, to communicate and inform clearly and frequently with key stakeholders within the business, and to foster and champion GKN’s 5 principles within sphere of influence.

**Required**
Role Qualifications
  
  

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification in Engineering (Aerospace, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials, Electrical, Chemical, or related discipline).
* Minimum of 8 years of experience in aerospace manufacturing or similar, highly regulated environments operating under AS9100 Quality Management Systems.
* Recent experience developing a manufacturing system for a New Product Introduction (NPI) with a comprehensive understanding of product lifecycle gate processes.
* Broad, hands-on experience with common manufacturing processes (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Knowledgeable of structured problem solving and RCCA methodologies (e.g. 8D) and how to apply these to complex problems.
* Demonstrated capability to organise and drive technical projects to achieve business goals, preferably in complex multi-site environments.
* Ability to lead and influence people, build trust and establish effective working relationships within a global organisation and with external customer stakeholders.
* Fluent in English language, both written and spoken.
* US Person for Export Control purposes

**Preferred**

* Demonstrated deployment of AS9145 APQP process.
* Working knowledge of digital systems for manufacturing (PLM, MES, ERP).
* Deep, expert knowledge in one or more manufacturing process areas (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Experience working with or for major aerospace OEMs and their systems.
* Proven ability to lead change in a Manufacturing System with evidence of delivering significant improvements in terms of cost, quality or throughput.
* Proven ability to identify and deliver industrial productivity improvements and monitor their efficacy by setting appropriate metrics.
* Project / Programme Management Professional Qualification.
* Six Sigma Certification.

Salary Range
  
  
$120-160k
  
  
We’ll offer you fantastic challenges and amazing opportunities. This is your chance to be part of an organisation that has proven itself to be at the cutting edge of our industry; and is committed to pushing the boundaries even further. And with some of the best training on offer in the industry, who knows how far you can go?
  
  
**A Great Place to work needs a Great Way of Working**
Everyone is welcome to apply to GKN. We believe that we can only achieve our ambitions through a coming together of diverse minds who enjoy collaborating in an inspirational environment. Through our commitment to diversity, inclusion and belonging and by living our five powerful principles we’ve created a culture where everyone feels welcome to contribute. It’s a culture that won us ‘The Best Workplace Culture Award’. By embracing and celebrating what makes us unique we encourage everyone to bring their full self to work.
  
  
We’re also committed to providing an accessible recruitment process, so if you require reasonable adjustments at any stage during our recruitment process please get in touch and let us know.
  
  
We are the place where human dreams, plus human endeavour, shape the future of aerospace innovation and technology.

existing_roles.title: Director, High Volume Production
existing_roles.description:
Please review the job details below.
  
  
Intuitive Machines - West is currently seeking a courageous, innovative, multi-skilled Director of High-Rate AIT Production to join our spacecraft production team in Palo Alto, CA.
  
  
**Life with Us**
Your Project: Intuitive Machines is a world leader in high-power spacecraft, having delivered some of the largest and highest-power spacecraft in the world. We are now looking to take this legacy of excellence to the next level, architecting a high-volume production line to build a large number of advanced spacecraft.
  
  
In this role, you will architect and implement a high-volume assembly, integration, and test (AIT) production line for these next-generation vehicles. You will be responsible for transforming our AIT operations from low-rate to high-rate production, establishing scalable processes and organizational capabilities to support our ambitious production targets. The scope includes complete spacecraft AIT from component receipt through final acceptance testing, encompassing electrical systems integration, solar array integration with the spacecraft bus, battery integration, advanced thermal solutions, and comprehensive environmental testing at production scale.
  
  
A critical aspect of this role is developing an efficient, right-sized test program—one that provides high confidence the vehicles will perform as designed while eliminating non-value-added test activities that add cost and schedule without commensurate risk reduction. You will apply rigorous engineering judgment to distinguish between essential verification activities and legacy testing practices that may not be necessary for production-rate vehicles.
  
  
We are looking for leaders to bravely challenge conventional AIT approaches and establish production-rate processes for these advanced systems. You will play an essential role in applying design-for-manufacturing/design-for-test (DFM/DFT) principles to develop AIT specifications and manufacturing plans suitable for volume production. Additionally, you will represent AIT capabilities during customer proposal efforts, providing technical credibility and instilling confidence in our ability to execute high-volume production of complex spacecraft.
  
  
Your Career: We're very serious about professional development and continuing education at Intuitive Machines - West. We offer our team members the opportunity to define their own career trajectory. You will work with your manager to set goals and design a development plan to advance your career. This unique opportunity is a high-visibility role critical to our company's leadership position in spacecraft manufacturing.
  
  
What We Offer: Time for dedicated professional development, conference attendance, industry training, peer group collaboration, as well as paid certifications and education reimbursement.
  
  
Who you will work with: You will report to the VP of Spacecraft Production and Operations and collaborate closely with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. You will lead a team of AIT production engineers and technicians while partnering with design engineering to ensure producibility of our spacecraft systems. You will also engage directly with potential customers during proposal phases to communicate our production and test capabilities.
  
  
**Your Responsibilities**

* Design end-to-end AIT production flow optimized for high-volume throughput
* Develop capacity models, takt time analysis, and process flow requirements for production-rate AIT
* Define capital equipment strategy including test equipment, handling systems, and tooling
* Establish scalable AIT work instructions, process controls, and quality gates
* Lead development of an efficient, risk-informed test program that ensures vehicle performance confidence while eliminating non-value-added testing
* Oversee spacecraft-level integration of solar arrays, batteries, and other major subsystems with the spacecraft bus
* Implement manufacturing execution systems (MES) tailored to provide assembly process documentation and production tracking for volume spacecraft production
* Define requirements for low-cost mechanical and electrical assembly, integration and test equipment, and production tooling
* Lead Voice of Manufacturing inputs to spacecraft design to ensure producibility at scale
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging lean manufacturing principles
* Build and mentor AIT production engineering team
* Represent AIT production capabilities to potential customers during proposal efforts, providing technical credibility on execution readiness
* Support business development with AIT cost models and production capacity commitments

**How You Will Be Evaluated**
Your performance will be measured against AIT production readiness milestones, test program efficiency metrics, production ramp targets, quality metrics, and cost per unit objectives.
  
  
**What We Look For In Team Members**
As a team member at Intuitive Machines - West, we expect you to demonstrate honesty, integrity, innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field. Four additional years of experience may be substituted for a degree
* Minimum of 15 years related aerospace manufacturing/AIT experience
* Minimum of 7 years leadership experience in production or manufacturing engineering
* Experience working cross-functionally within a company and/or with external partners and contractors
* Proven track record scaling aerospace production operations
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with volume production of spacecraft or complex aerospace systems
* Direct experience developing and implementing a spacecraft AIT production line
* Experience with large spacecraft systems (solar array integration, battery integration, high-voltage testing)
* Demonstrated experience developing efficient, risk-based test programs that balance verification rigor with schedule/cost efficiency
* Understanding of spacecraft environmental testing at production scale (thermal vacuum, vibration, EMI/EMC)
* Prior history as an AIT engineer, process engineer, or industrial engineer for aerospace products
* Experience with sustaining engineering processes such as Change Approval, NPI, breakpointing
* Advanced degree in a technical field
* Lean/Six Sigma certification
* Experience with AS9100 quality systems
* Capital project management experience (multi-million dollar equipment investments)
* Experience taking spacecraft products into production, including progressive design iterations to reduce delivered cost
* Demonstrated experience applying system engineering practices to AIT operations
* Excellent communication and presentation skills, with experience engaging directly with customers in technical/proposal settings
* Experience working directly with customers in the commercial space industry
* Ability to work independently with a high degree of organization and attention to detail

existing_roles.title: Manager / Senior Manager, Technical Operations
existing_roles.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with
**neffy®**
, the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.
  
  
**THE OPPORTUNITY**
The Manager / Sr. Manager, Technical Operations will play a key role in executing Technical Operations programs that support the continued development and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical judgment, project management, and external partner leadership in a highly collaborative environment.
  
  
Working closely with internal stakeholders and CMOs, this role provides technical and operational leadership across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Responsibilities include leading Technical Operations projects, supporting formulation and process development, technology transfer, GMP manufacturing activities, and resolution of technical and operational issues. The position ensures project scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, and budgets remain aligned while proactively identifying and escalating risks to support compliant, reliable, and on-time product supply.
  
  
**Essential Duties & Responsibilities**

* Manage cross-functional Technical Operations projects and day-to-day technical and operational interactions with assigned external partners, including scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, key milestones, project meetings, action tracking, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and CMO/vendor performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., service, quality, delivery, capacity, and right-first-time).
* Serve as a Technical Operations point of contact for assigned external manufacturing partners and work closely with CMOs and internal stakeholders to ensure execution against agreed project plans and supply requirements.
* Provide technical oversight of formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, and continued process verification activities, as applicable.
* Plan and support clinical and commercial manufacturing campaigns in coordination with CMOs, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and other internal functions; provide on-site/person-in-plant support for key manufacturing activities as needed.
* Review manufacturing and process documentation, including master and executed batch records, protocols, reports, process performance data, vendor change controls, investigations, and annual/product reviews, for technical accuracy and process performance.
* Lead or support technical assessment and resolution of manufacturing deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and other process issues; contribute to root-cause analysis and appropriate corrective and preventive actions in partnership with Quality Assurance.
* Assess proposed manufacturing and process changes for technical impact and support cross-functional evaluation of quality, supply, and regulatory implications.
* Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.
* Support vendor selection, onboarding, and qualification activities in collaboration with Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Procurement, and other stakeholders.
* Communicate project status, technical risks, manufacturing issues, and recommend actions clearly to Technical Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; escalate significant issues to appropriate decision-makers.
* Support preparation and review of CMC information for regulatory submissions and responses to health authority questions, as required.
* Support Technical Operations process improvement, business continuity, capacity planning, and other strategic operational initiatives as assigned.
* Support commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including coordination with third-party logistics (3PL) providers, distribution partners, and external manufacturing/packaging partners to maintain reliable product supply.
* Support product serialization activities, including EPCIS data exchange and operational compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements, working with packaging, distribution, Quality Assurance, and other partners as appropriate.
* Support clinical supply activities, including coordination with Clinical Operations and external vendors for clinical packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities, as applicable.

**Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities**

* Strong working knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, and applicable quality systems and regulatory expectations.
* Demonstrated technical understanding of formulation, manufacturing processes, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, and process performance sufficient to critically evaluate CMO data and recommendations, work effectively in cross-functional technical teams, and hold external partners accountable to commitments.
* Strong project and vendor management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, timelines, deliverables, and external partners in a fast-paced environment.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex manufacturing or process issues, develop recommendations, and communicate the rationale for action.
* Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across functions and organizational levels, including senior management and external partners.
* Well-organized, detail-oriented, and able to identify and escalate risks while maintaining focus on execution and business priorities.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project/reporting tools; experience with project management, continuous improvement, or operational excellence methodologies is a plus.
* Working knowledge of commercial and clinical supply operations relevant to Technical Operations, including 3PL interfaces, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA requirements, and clinical IRT/IWRS processes; direct experience in one or more of these areas is preferred.
* Must be able to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 20% to support external manufacturing partners and key project activities.

**Education And Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, chemical engineering, engineering, or a related scientific/technical discipline; an advanced degree is a plus. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered.
* Minimum of 5 years of relevant pharmaceutical/biotechnology experience in Technical Operations, manufacturing, process/formulation development, CMC, supply chain, or a related function.
* Experience working with external CMOs/CDMOs and supporting GMP clinical and/or commercial manufacturing is strongly preferred.
* Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, commercial product launch, or PPQ is preferred.
* Experience reviewing manufacturing batch records and process documentation and supporting technical investigations, change controls, and regulatory CMC activities is preferred.
* Experience supporting commercial distribution/3PL operations, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA compliance, and/or clinical supply and IRT/IWRS activities is preferred.

The full-time salary range for this posted position is $140,000 to $175,000 and may be eligible for a discretionary annual performance bonus. Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and other job-related factors permitted by law.
  
  
*This position is also eligible for Equity, 401k matching, and our excellent benefits package including 100% employer paid Medical, Dental & Vision for employees. View the full package here: ARS Careers Page*
